$comment: Packet documents remain independently versioned at packetcraftr.packet/v1.
title: PacketcraftR command output v4
description: Aggregate JSON and sequenced NDJSON. Every stream record declares event in its envelope; complete and error are terminal.

sequence.description: Zero-based ordinal of this emitted NDJSON record within one command invocation. Records are contiguous, and domain identifiers remain in result or error context.

event.description: Stream record discriminator; complete and error terminate the stream.

fragments.description: Capture-global fragment accounting; derived bytes are separate from the physical matched frame and byte totals.

ipDatagramKey.description: Capture-scoped identity of one fragmented IPv4 or IPv6 datagram.

ipReassemblyReport.description: Capture-global fragment counters and bounded completed or incomplete datagram outcomes.

tlsResult.description: Every assembled TLS session the selectors kept, plus the pass counters.

sessions.description: Sessions in first-seen order, bounded by --max-tls-sessions; summary.sessions_omitted reports what that ceiling left out.

tlsStatus.description: How far a handshake got, and why it stopped. Exactly one status is reported per session.

oneOf.description: A ClientHello and its matching ServerHello were both assembled.
A ClientHello was assembled and the connection ended before any ServerHello.
A HelloRetryRequest was assembled and the connection ended before the real ServerHello.
A fatal alert in the clear ended the handshake.
Record or handshake bytes could not be parsed, or one direction's buffer reached its ceiling.
Handshake bytes were missing: reassembly reported a gap, a resource ceiling retired the session, or the capture started mid-handshake.
The capture ended while the handshake was still in flight.

tlsAlert.description: One alert record observed in the clear. A TLS 1.3 alert sent after the ServerHello is encrypted and therefore invisible.

description_name.description: The registered AlertDescription name, or null for an unregistered code point.

tlsClient.description: What one client offered. Lists keep wire order and include GREASE code points. Fingerprints are advisory: every byte they are computed from is chosen by the client.

sni.description: The offered server name, null when absent or rejected as invalid.

sni_raw_hex.description: The raw host_name bytes, kept whenever the entry was present.

sni_is_outer.description: Whether sni is the outer, public name of an Encrypted ClientHello.

cipher_suite_name.description: The registered cipher suite name, or null for an unregistered code point.

alpn.description: The selected ALPN protocol. TLS 1.3 moves ALPN into the encrypted extensions, so this is populated for TLS 1.2 and below only.

tlsSession.description: One assembled TLS handshake, joining a client's offer to a server's decision.

session.description: Monotonic zero-based index in first-seen order, unique for the run.

tcp_stream.description: The tcp.stream conversation index this handshake rode on. A four-tuple reused after a clean close carries several sessions on one stream.

handshake_rtt_ms.description: Milliseconds between the frame completing the ClientHello and the frame completing the ServerHello, when both were captured. Negative when the ServerHello frame is timestamped before the ClientHello frame, which capture clocks do produce.

alerts_dropped.description: Alerts seen past the per-session cap and not listed in alerts. Absent when none were dropped.

reason.description: Why the status is what it is, for malformed, gap, and truncated.

tlsStatusCounts.description: Sessions per terminal status. Every status is reported, so a zero is a statement rather than a missing key.

sessions.description: Sessions assembled, of every status, whether or not a selector kept them.

sessions_selected.description: Sessions that passed the command's selectors.

tcp_streams.description: TCP conversations seen, whether or not they carried TLS.

sessions_evicted.description: Sessions retired by a resource ceiling rather than by the capture.

sessions_omitted.description: Selected sessions left out of the aggregate because it reached its retention ceiling. Non-zero only in the JSON aggregate; text and NDJSON write each session as it completes and omit nothing.

udp_443_frames.description: UDP frames seen on port 443, which are most likely QUIC. TLS over QUIC is out of scope, so this is how under-reporting stays visible.

tlsCodePoint.description: An IANA TLS registry code point, kept numeric and authoritative.

exchangeStreamSuccess.description: One progressive exchange event. Sent records follow provider-confirmed transmission, capture evidence follows definitive classification, unanswered records follow successful capture completion, and complete is terminal.

fuzzCaseSuccess.description: One progressive fuzz case or the single terminal complete event. Case index is deterministic domain identity and does not select envelope sequence.

parent.description: Protocol whose binding reaches this one during dissection

discriminator.description: Selector value the parent matches: a port, EtherType, or protocol number; zero is the parent's fallback

ipAddress.description: Validators must enable JSON Schema format assertions to enforce IP address syntax.

operationStats.description: Command-processed counters. For capture, packets_attempted is the one-based source-frame count, packets_completed is the matched/emitted frame count, and bytes is captured source bytes; capture contains distinct provider-reported backend statistics.

captureStatistics.description: Capture-provider counters reported by the backend; these can differ from command-processed counters when filtering, queueing, or provider loss occurs.

sourceFrame.description: One-based source-frame identity supplied to display filters as frame.number; filtering does not renumber it.
